questions.q: What is the key difference between traditional programming and machine learning?
options: In traditional programming you write the rules; in machine learning the algorithm learns the rules from data and answers
Traditional programming uses data, machine learning does not
Machine learning never needs any data
Traditional programming can only be written in SQL
questions.explain: Traditional code: rules + data give answers. Machine learning: data + answers give rules, which we call a model.

questions.q: In the house-price example, what plays the role of the target (label)?
options: Square footage
The price
The random seed
The intercept
questions.explain: The target is the answer we want to predict: the price. Square footage is the feature.

questions.q: What does calling model.fit(X, y) do?
options: Predicts prices for new houses
Deletes rows with missing values
Learns the model's numbers from the training examples
Splits the data into train and test sets
questions.explain: fit is training: the algorithm adjusts its internal numbers (here a slope and an intercept) to match the examples.

questions.q: What is the real measure of whether a model is any good?
options: How well it fits the data it was trained on
How many lines of code it takes
How complicated the algorithm is
How well it performs on new data it has never seen
questions.explain: A model that only memorizes its training data is useless. Performance on unseen data is what matters.

questions.q: For which situation is machine learning the WRONG tool?
options: Predicting churn from thousands of past customers
Applying a fixed 10% discount to every order over $500
Estimating house prices from many features
Spotting unusual transactions in a huge log
questions.explain: When a clear, stable rule already does the job, write the rule. ML is for patterns too complex or changing to hand-code.
